paragraphs:
R. Matya ben Ḥarash, Avot 4; Mishnah Yoma 8:6. 'Justice, justice shall you pursue': go after Matya to Rome, Sanhedrin 32b; see Yose ben Kisma. A gloss on Maimonides, end of Sanhedrin 6, says no court in his time was greater than his. When he left for outside the Land, he tore his clothes; see R. Yehudah ben Beteira and Ḥananyah [son of] R. Yehoshua’s brother. Yoma 4b: the words of Yose the Galilean; Akiva says, etc.; Natan says, etc.; Matya ben Ḥarash says. R. Eliezer the Great was his teacher, as Me'ilah states. He sent to R. Elazar ben Azaryah concerning the four divisions of atonement, end of Yoma 86. He studied Torah with R. Yoshiyah, who turned to worldly affairs. He told him, 'My teacher, why leave the words of the living God, although you are my teacher and I your student?' Avot deRabbi Natan, beginning of chapter 1. Chapter 29 has Matya ben Ḥarash visit R. Yishmael ben Elazar HaKappar in Laodicea. But Mekhilta, Yitro, BaḤodesh HaShelishi 7, has him go to R. Elazar HaKappar in Lodya and address him as 'My teacher.' He asked whether he had heard the four divisions of atonement expounded by Yishmael. He answered, 'I heard; they are three, and repentance accompanies each.' At the end of Yoma and in Nedarim he spoke in Yishmael's name (see his entry). He addressed R. Natan as 'My teacher,' Avot deRabbi Natan 1. R. Shimon ben Yoḥai found him in Rome and asked about the four divisions of atonement, etc.; Matya appears to have been older. Yoma 53b has him ask him, etc.; Me'ilah 17a has him ask R. Shimon ben Yoḥai the source for creeping creatures' blood being impure. R. Yishmael son of R. Yose said three things in his name.

Yalkut, Vayeḥi, citing Midrash Avkir: Matya ben Ḥarash sat studying Torah in the study house. His face shone like the sun and his appearance resembled the ministering angels, for he had never raised his eyes to a woman. Once Satan passed, envied him, and asked whether such a person could never have sinned. He asked the Holy One how Matya stood before Him; He answered that he was wholly righteous. Satan requested permission to tempt him. He answered, 'You cannot overcome him,' yet told him to go. Satan appeared as a woman of beauty unequaled since Na'amah, Tuval Kayin's sister, through whom the angels erred, as 'the sons of God saw the daughters of man.' He stood before Matya, who turned away. He stood on the left, and Matya turned right, turning to every side. Matya feared his impulse might overcome him and cause sin. He called his attendant student to bring fire and a nail; he brought them, and Matya put them into his eyes. Satan shuddered and fell backward. The Holy One summoned Raphael to heal Matya. Raphael stood before him and identified himself as sent to heal his eyes. Matya answered, 'Leave me; what happened has happened.' Raphael returned and reported. God sent him back to guarantee that the evil impulse would not rule him; immediately he healed him. End of quotation.

Matya was Palti ben Layish, who took Mikhal daughter of Shaul and planted a sword between himself and her. Nevertheless he should not have kept her, but should have told Shaul he refused her; where God's name is desecrated, one does not honor a teacher. Of him it says, 'You drive My people's women from their pleasant homes.' Though he did not touch her, he enjoyed looking, feeding his eyes on what was not his. He now wished to repair this, afflicted himself and blinded his eyes. For this he was handed to Satan's temptation, etc.; he strengthened himself against his impulse and refused to look at her face, etc. Both Palti and Matya were sparks of Yosef the righteous—Gilgulei Neshamot. He is buried in Ilavon, in stone—גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael]. His sons: R. Elazar, R. Yehoshua and R. Yoḥanan. R. Assi ben Matya.
